title: The Secrets of Quantitative Investing - ft. Simon Judes - Top Traders Unplugged 139

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/The Secrets of Quantitative Investing - ft. Simon Judes - Top Traders Unplugged 139.docx

summary:
Judes explains Winton's scientific research approach, three-quarters trend plus one-quarter other signals, why long-term trend Sharpe is about 0.5 and fast trends deteriorated most.
Adds that more genuinely diversifying markets matter via effective number of markets, risk is not volatility, and trend is often contrarian.
Conclusions: no regime-based speed switching, humans own key parameters, scenario stress tests from history and correlation shocks.

completeness_estimate: 0.82 - first reader's 46 claims cover the core Winton method, speed, markets, risk and contrarian-trend arguments; additions are secondary reasoning (allocator mechanism, research structure, correlation condition, caveats).

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: what matters is original research to find new Alpha sources and you know improve our existing ones and on risk management
claims.claim: Winton's priorities are original research for new alpha sources and improvement of existing ones, plus hyper-vigilant risk management that monitors many possible scenarios.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's a diversified CTA which is three-quarters Trend following and a quarter other systematic microstrategies and then we have pure Trend products as well
claims.claim: Winton runs a diversified CTA that is 75% trend following and 25% other systematic macro strategies, alongside pure trend and quant multi-strategy products.
claims.testable: partly - mix is a design choice testable via backtest

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: people have been very influenced by their initial experiences
claims.claim: Researchers' and firms' early market experiences (1987, 2008) shape how they parametrise and organise trend strategies, a behavioural source of differences between trend followers.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you can discover and improve successful investment strategies by applying empirical scientific research methods
claims.claim: Winton's philosophy is to approach markets with an open mind and use empirical scientific research, rejecting the efficient market hypothesis as a foundation, because good predictions are possible with hard work.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: help you in particular test multiple hypotheses at the same time and sometimes also sequentially one after the other
claims.claim: Avoiding data-mining false positives requires shared statistical techniques for testing many hypotheses simultaneously and sequentially, which also drives hiring and training.
claims.testable: yes - apply multiple-testing corrections to trial counts

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: avoiding situations where researchers privately overfit ideas and day touring and then only show you
claims.claim: Process must prevent researchers from privately overfitting many ideas and presenting only the subset that looked good in a backtest.
claims.testable: yes - log all trials and count them

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: if there is for example an economic rationale behind a particular idea then you can use that you can test the intermediate economic relationships and that can add additional confidence
claims.claim: Backtest statistics give confidence in Sharpe and low correlation, and an economic rationale with testable intermediate relationships adds confidence; absence of a rationale lowers confidence rather than killing the idea.
claims.indicator: backtest Sharpe, correlation to existing strategies

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: extremely diverse collection of alpha sources
claims.claim: Winton's alpha comes from a mixture of behavioural, structural and microstructure sources depending on strategy, so it is hard to say who is on the other side of the trades.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the long-term sharp outlook for Trend following is perhaps around a half
claims.claim: Harding's 2018 view is that long-term trend following Sharpe is around 0.5, enough on its own to run a fund only marginally, so other signals should be added to raise Sharpe.
claims.testable: yes - Sharpe of trend indices over time

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: then you actually find a consistent decline in the performance of trend um of the kind of trend strategies that people were trading at the time
claims.claim: Over a long window from the 1970s trend performance declined steadily for the strategies in use; the decline was first seen in Winton research around 2007 and was not just a post-2008 story.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: instead of having one product uh dominated by Trend following we now have three products
claims.claim: Winton responded to lower trend Sharpe expectations by splitting into pure trend, diversified CTA and multi-strategy products rather than abandoning trend.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: I think we prefer to look at the investor experience you look at situations where investors really needed diversification in 2008 uh last year and trend has done very well there
claims.claim: Trend gave diversification in 2008 and 2022, but the long drawdowns in between make allocators drop it; judging by investor experience beats focusing on Sharpe or mandate labels.
claims.testable: yes - trend vs equity drawdown episodes

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's Great Value in adding signals which smooth out those drawdowns
claims.claim: Adding non-trend signals smooths drawdowns but reduces crisis effectiveness, so type and weight of added signals matter; Winton chooses 75% trend as the level that keeps the trend profile with some drift.
claims.conditions: depends on which signals are added and their weight

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it needs to have um you know it needs to be opportunistic so that you you don't you're not stuck in the same asset class or in the same Market you can move around
claims.claim: Kaminski's crisis alpha traits: liquid, opportunistic (can move to where the action is) and unbiased (long as easily as short); in 2020 the best trade was long bonds and short energy, in 2022 the opposite.
claims.testable: partly - trade direction by year documented

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: those three characteristics that you mentioned are prerequisites for something to function in that way but they don't guarantee that it's going to work
claims.claim: Liquidity, opportunism and no bias are necessary, not sufficient, for crisis performance; trend does well in extended trends but fails when equities rise steadily then reverse sharply (Feb 2018).
claims.conditions: after a steady equity rise followed by a sharp downturn
claims.testable: yes - trend returns around Feb 2018 type reversals

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the best thing is to really try and describe the strategy how it's going to react what it's going to do in different environments
claims.claim: Labels like crisis alpha mislead because trend only sometimes works in crises; describe its response in different environments instead.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: even if you um can't time Trend following even if we agree that you can't time when it's going to work there's still a risk for the allocator
claims.claim: Trend cannot be timed, but allocators bear personal risk if it underperforms right after they allocate, so concerns should be addressed rather than answered with statistics.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's no reason to think that next year will be um will be bad because last year was good
claims.claim: A good year does not predict a bad next year: 2008 was good but all prior Winton years were also good, and good years come in sequences; investors can average in over months to ease timing worries.
claims.testable: yes - autocorrelation of annual CTA returns

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we don't trade it on um equities um though because often that that does just add a long bias to your Equity portfolio
claims.claim: Carry added to trend is not traded in equities because it adds long equity bias and reduces convexity; carry's currency-style small-gain/large-loss profile is mitigated by trading it in commodities and fixed income too.
claims.direction: carry returns smoother across commodities and bonds than currencies
claims.conditions: equities excluded because of long bias

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: important to you know fix a level so that investors know what they're what they're going to get
claims.claim: The trend/non-trend mix depends on the opportunity set but is fixed so investors know what they receive.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the largest deterioration is seen in the faster Trend strategies this is what everyone was trading
claims.claim: Fast trend strategies deteriorated most since 1997 because everyone traded them; slow strategies started with lower Sharpe, so always choosing the best speed shows decline.
claims.direction: fast trend Sharpe down, slow flat

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: if you're trying to purely maximize the the sharp ratio um then uh what our analysis has shown is that you really want to be very slow
claims.claim: Maximising Sharpe alone favours very slow trend, but investors want responsiveness at turning points like 2008 and 2022, so some faster speed fits objectives even at lower Sharpe.
claims.conditions: investor objective is crisis responsiveness not Sharpe

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: one place we uh we haven't uh looked so much recently though is is in academic journals actually
claims.claim: Winton finds academic journals no longer at the forefront of alpha research and instead does original research, sometimes finding ideas from Chinese commodity markets that work globally.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: often adjustments to our our volatility models for example have been prompted by new types of events
claims.claim: Event-driven model adjustments: Feb 2007's reversal that hit CTA positions (crowding effect) led to volatility model changes that helped in Feb 2018.
claims.indicator: CTA volatility models, Feb 2007 and Feb 2018 reversals
claims.direction: CTA losses in sudden reversals after low-volatility equity rises
claims.conditions: after rising equities on low volatility

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: if on the other hand you took a month to turn around your positions then you lost all the way down and then you lost again on the way up
claims.claim: Fast trend beat slow in Feb-Mar 2020 because the fall lasted one month before the Fed stepped in; Winton saw no evidence of a lasting change and slower trend has since done better again.
claims.indicator: fast vs slow trend in March 2020
claims.direction: fast trend gained in a one-month crash

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you can see that this apparently technical statistical decision about which is the best speed at that moment amounts to just a call on what the FED is going to do and when
claims.claim: Switching trend speed with the regime is an implicit call on policy (e.g. Fed intervention), which systematic managers should not make; discretionary macro managers do that.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: machine learning algorithms require a lot of data a lot of training data
claims.claim: Machine learning lacks enough independent events for slow-trading strategies because few examples of crashes exist, but works for faster intraday strategies with many observations.
claims.conditions: slow time scales fail, fast time scales work

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: in financial markets if you're talking about what happens on slower time scales how you deal with events like a market crash well you can't just create a market crash on demand
claims.claim: Slow-horizon research is an observational science (cannot rerun a crash) while fast execution research is experimental and can iterate, so machine learning suits the latter.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we're fairly Universal but they're not not completely there are practical differences often between uh between markets
claims.claim: Parameters are mostly universal across markets but adjusted for transaction cost, market impact, spreads and commissions.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: our point of view has generally been that we try to push responsibility on the human fairly early so things like the trend following speed
claims.claim: Humans should own early design decisions such as trend speed and asset allocation (made with analysis) rather than defer to an optimizer, preserving understanding of the portfolio.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: I think they are a single manager if you want to mitigate a single manager risk then obviously the fund of funds approach is the way to go
claims.claim: Regression-based CTA replication (about 95bp fee) is still a single-manager risk; Winton disagrees that it mitigates manager risk.

correction.issue: The fee figure was supplied by the host, not Judes: Judes asked how much replication products charge and the host answered 'just shy of one percent' (85bp plus about 10bp). Judes' own view is only that replication does not mitigate single-manager risk and that fund-of-funds is the real route.
correction.fix: Judes disagrees that regression-based CTA replication mitigates single-manager risk (the replicator is itself a single manager; fund of funds is the way to diversify manager risk); the host noted such products charge just under 1% (about 95bp).

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the number that goes into that square root is not the number of markets you trade but the effective number of markets when you've taken account of all of the correlations
claims.claim: Sharpe scales with the square root of the effective number of markets given correlations; 50-60 markets might be only 8-10 independent, so adding genuinely different markets adds a lot.
claims.conditions: adding highly correlated markets adds nothing

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the alternative markets portfolio they did extremely well in that period
claims.claim: Alternative markets outperformed major markets over the last decade, including the post-crisis period when mainstream trend struggled; European gas and power gave huge trends (gas up tenfold).
claims.direction: alternative market trend returns above major markets

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the markets that you add have to genuinely be alternative and additive
claims.claim: Added markets should be truly diversifying (Chinese futures, regional gas, power, freight, marine fuel) rather than equity sector ETFs or developed-market swaps correlated with existing exposure.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's still markets that where you can clear your position uh on the exchange so you can um really reduce the counterparty risk
claims.claim: Many OTC-traded alternative markets can be cleared on exchange, reducing counterparty risk close to major futures levels.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: these markets are by definition have a barrier to entry and that's you know one of the reasons why they have extra offers
claims.claim: Alternative markets carry extra returns partly because barriers to entry (software, operations, middle office) keep trend followers from extending into them easily.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the answers depend on what the investors objectives are what their tolerance is for for drawdowns in particular parts of their book
claims.claim: Trend allocation size and form (pure, capped beta) depend on the investor's drawdown tolerance and process, so there is no fixed rule; customised programs often vary alternative-market or China exposure rather than trend share.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's a strange confusion that affects the CTA industry particularly which is to equate risk with volatility
claims.claim: Risk is not volatility: in 2017 the VIX was at record lows while valuations were rich, and estimating loss risk is harder than estimating volatility, so use many risk measures besides volatility.
claims.testable: partly - compare vol vs drawdown predictors

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we look at our current positions and we see how they would have performed in all the previous Market environments that we have data for
claims.claim: Risk management by replaying current positions through all historical environments (worst day or week) and asking whether the loss is acceptable, e.g. the 1990 Gulf War oil jump of 30%.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: most things are short bonds and long equities so obviously the um the situation that's really worrisome is a very classic risk-off move where bonds rally inequities um decline
claims.claim: In early 2023 trend positions were short bonds and long equities, so a risk-off move with bonds rallying and equities falling (disinflationary bad news) is the main scenario risk.
claims.direction: portfolio losses if bonds up, equities down

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the way that these strategies operate the leverage naturally fluctuates as the signal strength varies and the correlation between markets varies
claims.claim: Leverage varies naturally with signal strength and correlations, and risk measures decide whether to hold it inside a band.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you look at things like what if all the correlations change in whatever way would be worse for you
claims.claim: Stylised stress test of correlation flips: before the 2013 taper tantrum trend was long bonds and long stocks with negative correlation, and a positive correlation scenario looked unacceptable, so risk was cut.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we temporarily operated at a lower level of volatility and that really helped us actually in that year
claims.claim: Winton ran lower volatility ahead of the 2013 taper tantrum because of the correlation scenario, which helped that year.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you reduce the long-term performance to some extent depending on how big the you know how significant the cap is
claims.claim: Capping equity long exposure in a trend program reduces long-term performance in proportion to the cap, helps crisis profile, and is offered as a bespoke option; neither is objectively better.
claims.direction: long-run return down, equity beta down

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you can diversify and you reduce the single manager risk and on the other hand you don't and have fee netting
claims.claim: Using multiple trend managers cuts single-manager risk but loses fee netting; the investor chooses the trade-off.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: it's clear that that correlates very strongly to the growth of people trading the strategy
claims.claim: The decline in trend performance correlates strongly with growth in the number of traders, so 0.5 Sharpe is the expectation; long simulations only show underlying markets trend, not future Sharpe for a crowded strategy.
claims.direction: Sharpe down as trend AUM up
claims.testable: yes - regress Sharpe on CTA AUM

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: Trend following is most successful it's because it's actually a contrarian strategy
claims.claim: Trend following is often contrarian to prevailing fundamental narratives, e.g. oil in 2014 when shale supply was underestimated against a peak-oil view.
claims.conditions: when fundamental narrative opposes the move

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: for that to be a trend the movement has to be extended in time and often it can be extended because it is contrarian because there's a narrative
claims.claim: Trends extend in time because a prevailing narrative says the market must go the other way, as in German yields that kept falling into negative territory against the belief they could never go below zero.
claims.conditions: when a widespread belief rejects the move

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my opinion is we probably should change the conversation to talk about the Improvement of portfolio shop that these strategies provide
claims.claim: Trend following should be judged by the improvement in total-portfolio Sharpe it delivers, not by its stand-alone Sharpe or a 'crisis alpha' mandate, because Sharpe was not created for single-strategy evaluation (reacting to the AQR paper on trend mandates).
claims.conditions: when trend is held alongside traditional assets
claims.testable: yes - marginal contribution to portfolio Sharpe can be computed

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: the people who are making these allocation decisions have to justify each line item to their investment committees and it becomes very difficult
claims.claim: Allocators abandon trend after long drawdowns not from lack of faith but because each line item must be justified to an investment committee, which is why smoothing the drawdowns has great value.
claims.conditions: when allocation decisions are scrutinised line by line
claims.testable: partly - allocator flows can be studied

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they kind of look at Trend following a little bit like a trade they try to time it and then also they have this notion that well it did so well in 2022 um it's either too late
claims.claim: Potential investors treat trend following as a tactical trade and assume that after a strong 2022 it is too late or cannot repeat, a market-timing mindset that trend followers need to counter.
claims.testable: partly - flows after good years can be checked

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: some of them are purely statistical in nature some of them have economic rationales some of them are other technical signals like Trend following that are different from Trend following
claims.claim: The non-trend quarter of the diversified CTA is a mixture of purely statistical signals, economic-rationale signals and non-trend technical signals, some faster than trend, with new signals added each year.
claims.indicator: non-trend signals in Winton diversified program

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: you've got your existing Alpha sources and you need to make sure you're doing them as well as you can and that involves reviewing things like the uh the speed of trend following
claims.claim: Research has two streams: finding new alpha sources (new ideas or data inputs) and maintaining existing ones by reviewing trend speed, signal construction and volatility models.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: there's a temptation as a um as a Quant to say everything's automated I didn't do anything the the whole thing's done by a computer that's definitely the wrong thing to do
claims.claim: Claiming that a systematic process is fully automated hides that someone must still choose the parameters or the algorithm that chooses them (an infinite regress), so firms should deliberately decide at which level humans take responsibility.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: a lot of the additional markets you see often are as you say financial markets that may have correlations to other markets that you may already have
claims.claim: Counterpoint to the more-markets argument: a 50-60 market classical portfolio already includes diversified commodities, and going from 100 to 200 markets mostly adds correlated financial markets unless the extras are genuinely alternative (e.g. Chinese futures).
claims.indicator: number of markets in trend portfolios
claims.direction: Sharpe gain from extra markets small beyond about 100
claims.conditions: when added markets are correlated financial instruments
claims.testable: yes - Sharpe vs effective number of markets

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we trade them now um via the internationalized markets via swaps and by the qfi route you know for our Global Investors
claims.claim: Chinese futures are accessed onshore, through internationalised exchange contracts, via swaps and via the QFI route, an execution method for reaching a diversifying market that others cannot easily trade.

claims.speaker: Simon Judes
claims.quote: we've been seeing sort of modest positive correlation between those asset classes and obviously the dynamic with with inflation has made that somewhat different from the usual situation
claims.claim: Recently stock-bond correlation has been modestly positive because of the inflation dynamic, so bonds no longer rally reliably in risk-off episodes and trend portfolios that are short bonds and long equities face a different scenario map.
claims.direction: bonds and equities fall together when inflation drives markets
claims.conditions: when inflation, not growth, is the dominant shock

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you've got lower trading costs now that you might have had in the past um which would be a positive and fees have probably come down for investors too
claims.claim: Lower trading costs and lower fees are partial offsets to the decline in gross trend Sharpe, so the investor's net outlook is less negative than the 0.5 gross estimate suggests.
claims.indicator: trend net Sharpe after costs and fees
claims.direction: net returns less depressed than gross
